## Problem

We want to fit a linear model $\hat{y} = w^\top x + b$ to data
$\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n}$ by minimizing the mean-squared error

$$
\mathcal{L}(w, b) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left( w^\top x_i + b - y_i \right)^2 .
$$ {#eq-loss}

## Gradients

Differentiating @eq-loss gives

$$
\nabla_w \mathcal{L} = \frac{2}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left( w^\top x_i + b - y_i \right) x_i,
\qquad
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial b} = \frac{2}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left( w^\top x_i + b - y_i \right).
$$ {#eq-grad}

and the update rule with learning rate $\eta$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{t+1} &= w_t - \eta \, \nabla_w \mathcal{L}(w_t, b_t) \\
b_{t+1} &= b_t - \eta \, \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial b}(w_t, b_t).
\end{aligned}
$$

## Implementation

```python
import numpy as np

def fit(X, y, lr=1e-2, steps=1_000):
    n, d = X.shape
    w, b = np.zeros(d), 0.0
    for _ in range(steps):
        err = X @ w + b - y          # residuals
        w -= lr * (2 / n) * X.T @ err  # see @eq-grad
        b -= lr * (2 / n) * err.sum()
    return w, b
```

## Convergence

For a convex, $L$-smooth loss, choosing $\eta \le 1/L$ guarantees

$$
\mathcal{L}(w_t) - \mathcal{L}(w^\star) \le \frac{\lVert w_0 - w^\star \rVert^2}{2 \eta t}.
$$
